criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.
Given the data files, when any tab renders, then its content comes from .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json read at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given .colaberry/manifest.json, when any tab is shown, then it displays how old the data is and warns when that age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a production change request, When the request is submitted, Then it must require human approval.
Given a denied approval, When the request is resubmitted, Then it must still require approval.
Trust: Every approval decision is logged for audit.
Given an action is taken, When it is logged, Then it must be retrievable in the audit log.
Given a decision is made, When it is logged, Then it must include the decision maker.
Trust: Every log entry is timestamped and immutable.
Given an incident, When AI analyzes it, Then it must provide a recommendation with a confidence score.
Given a recommendation, When it is viewed, Then it must include evidence-backed reasoning.
Trust: All recommendations are logged with confidence scores.
Given an incident with low confidence, When additional diagnostics are gathered, Then they must be presented to the user.
Given multiple diagnostics, When they are presented, Then they must include possible causes.
Trust: All diagnostics gathering is logged.
Given a user role, When accessing the dashboard, Then it must display role-specific information.
Given an IT Manager, When viewing the dashboard, Then it must show operational summaries.
Trust: Dashboard access is logged by user role.

stories.notes: IT Manager role reshapes real DMV data into operational counts (incidents, blocked sessions); unrecognized roles rejected with 400, never rendered wrong. New frontend/ (Vite+React+TS) fetches via a dev-only Vite proxy, no CORS added to the backend. Every dashboard access logged by role. Verified end-to-end in a real browser against both real servers, not just unit-tested.

criteria.text: Given the system is connected to SQL Server, when a user requests a recommendation, then the system provides an AI-driven recommendation using SQL Server data.
Given the system is unable to connect to SQL Server, when a user requests a recommendation, then the system notifies the user of the connectivity issue.
Trust: All data access attempts are logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Verified against a real, live Azure SQL Database (Free tier), not just mocked — the R2/R3 gap this repo has carried since before this session ("the live path has never actually succeeded against a real SQL Server instance") is now closed. Found and fixed a real bug only discoverable live: the DMV query ordered by cpu_time DESC alone, which silently buried a genuine blocking scenario under 40-50+ Azure background system sessions (all near-zero CPU by definition of being blocked, not computing). Fixed query + regression test guard it. generateRecommendation() calls queryLiveDmv() directly (bypassing dmvReader.ts fallback) so an unreachable SQL Server notifies the user honestly rather than silently substituting fixture data and calling it real.

criteria.text: Given the system is connected to cloud services, when a user requests a recommendation, then the system provides an AI-driven recommendation using cloud service data.
Given the system is unable to connect to cloud services, when a user requests a recommendation, then the system notifies the user of the connectivity issue.
Trust: All data access attempts are logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Cloud-service counterpart to STORY-006's SQL Server path, same shape: cloudBlobSource.ts (real Azure Blob Storage I/O, timeout + capped retry + its own circuit breaker, separate failure domain from the DMV path) feeds cloudRecommendationService.ts (zod-validates each record before treating it as evidence, never falls back to fixture data and calls it real), wired to a new GET /api/cloud-recommendation route. Verified against a real, live Azure Blob Storage account (coreopsdiagnostics / diagnostics container), not just mocked. Positive case: real HTTP round trip read a real diagnostics.json blob and produced a real Claude recommendation (intentionally low-confidence / insufficientEvidence: true, since the single test record genuinely lacks root-cause detail — an honest result, not a bug). Negative case: a second server instance pointed at a nonexistent container returned a real 503 CLOUD_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, not a hang or a fabricated result. Trust: both the success and the failure attempt produced a cloud_recommendation_data_access log line in the server's own stderr output.

Given the system is unable to connect to cloud services, when a user requests a recommendation, then the system notifies the user of the connectivity issue.

criteria.text: Given a server, When monitoring is enabled, Then incidents must be detected continuously.
Given an incident, When detected, Then it must trigger an alert.
Trust: All monitoring actions are logged.

stories.notes: "A server" read as the one already-connected real system this repo can reach (the live Azure SQL Database from STORY-006) rather than a new, uncredentialed Windows Server connection — flagged and confirmed with the user before building. monitoringService.ts's startMonitoring()/stop() runs a real interval loop over queryLiveDmv() (never dmvReader.ts's fixture-fallback — a fabricated incident/all-clear would be exactly what STORY-006/007 refused). Incident = any row with a non-zero blocking_session_id, reusing STORY-006's already-fixed detection query as-is. A failed cycle is logged and the loop keeps running rather than dying; a logging failure is guarded so it can't take the loop down either. Wired to GET/POST /api/monitoring/{start,stop,status} in httpServer.ts, idempotent start/stop (calling start while already running does not spin up a second interval). Live testing surfaced and fixed a real bug before shipping: the interval fired on a fixed schedule regardless of whether the previous cycle had finished, and a cold-starting Azure SQL free-tier instance took ~30s to respond against the 10s default interval — overlapping cycles piled up concurrent connection attempts and tripped the shared circuit breaker on a false alarm. Fixed with an in-flight guard (skip a tick if the previous cycle hasn't finished) plus a regression test.

outstanding: Given a server, When monitoring is enabled, Then incidents must be detected continuously.
Given an incident, When detected, Then it must trigger an alert.
Trust: All monitoring actions are logged.

criteria.text: Given an incident with low confidence, When escalated, Then it must notify a human operator.
Given an escalation, When it occurs, Then it must be logged with the confidence score.
Trust: All escalations are logged with timestamps.

stories.notes: REQ-011 is source-agnostic ("escalate when confidence is below 60%", no system named), so built as a standalone evaluator (evaluateEscalation()) rather than rebuilding detection per source, then wired into both existing recommendation paths (STORY-006 SQL, STORY-007 cloud) via GET /api/recommendation and /api/cloud-recommendation — the story's own "reuse, don't rebuild" list only named STORY-007/008, but REQ-011 doesn't scope by source, so both were included; flagged to the user before building, confirmed. "Notify a human operator" (criterion 1) is a distinct, real logged event (escalation_triggered, warn level, notifiedOperator: true) — the same walking-skeleton meaning STORY-008 gave "alert"; a paging/email channel is explicitly STORY-010's job, not this one. Confidence < 60 escalates and logs with the score + an ISO timestamp (criteria 2 and 3, satisfied by one log line, same pattern STORY-008 used). Confidence >= 60 correctly returns null with no log call — tested explicitly, not assumed ("Escalation not triggered" failure path, boundary-tested at exactly 59/60). A malformed confidence score (NaN, negative, >100, +-Infinity) throws a typed InvalidConfidenceScoreError rather than silently escalating or silently not ("Incorrect confidence score"). The log call is guarded the same way STORY-008's was, so a logging hiccup can't silently swallow an escalation or crash the caller ("Escalation log failure").

outstanding: Given an incident with low confidence, When escalated, Then it must notify a human operator.
Given an escalation, When it occurs, Then it must be logged with the confidence score.
Trust: All escalations are logged with timestamps.
